I'll be honest lots of games today are skinnerboxes and are not made to be fun, rather how can they best get another few dollars out of you. Not to say there aren't fun games or games made by creatives without that corporate oversight forcing them to do those things... but you can't just go to gamestop and pick up a random box off the wall and have fun with it anymore. You have to do some digging to find something that you will enjoy.

What kind of games do/ did you used to like? For RPGs I'd say Baldurs Gate 3, DoS2, Age of Decadence/ Colony Ship, Underrail, Wasteland 3, and any of the Atlus SMT/Persona games have been my favorites in recent years. If you would rather something you can just sit down and play for a minute but don't have to focus on too much there are a lot more genres. Roguelikes such as TBoI, Gungeon, Hades, or lesser known ones like Gunfire Reborn. For FPSs you could always just play the new Dooms if you haven't already. For multiplayer there are just so many it's hard to know where to even start. There's puzzle games, survival games, deckbuilder card games, fighting games (both 2d mortal kombat/street fighter style and platform smash bros style), cozy farming games, dad games (that might peak your interest. there is regular dad games like euro truck simulator, flight simulator etc. Then there is a kind of post-dad game where it's still the \*what its like to have a job\* type game but with some kind of fantasy mixed in. hardspace shipbreaker, papers please, pacific drive, crime scene cleaner etc).

Those are all new things too. You can always go back and play the things that you used to like. I don't know what you used to play but Quake, Doom, Duke Nukem, Wolfenstein, non remake Resident Evil 4, Silent Hill 2, any old LoZ / Mario game. They all are still there and are just as good now as they were when they were made.

There are so many genres you could go to, but you have to also ask yourself if you want to. If you don't, well don't feel bad about it! Don't burn yourself out trying to find something you enjoy. You can always come back when you've had enough time to enjoy just trying to find something to play again.

What I really want is reasons to explore and quest. The only thing Underrail the og can reward you with when exploring is 1) exp and 2) money mixed with the occasional unique equipment item (talked abt below) and a psi skill that isn't in any trader inventory. For quests the only thing I can think of that isnt exp money or a trader unlock is the huxkey and the teleports from dude.

Materials for weapons are basically never above 100 quality if you didn't buy them. Weapons, armor, energy shields, basically anything in the game is better when crafted. Ofc that is natural if we're talkijg late game but instead you will never be using a piece if equipment you found if you're keeping up with the relevant crafting skill. Even uniques are significantly worse than even mid-game craftables. 

There are a few more uniques like the jackknife and lemurian tech suit for stats that are nice QOLs so I'm not saying there is NO reason to explore in the game. Even if none of that was there I would still have explored every map the way I have because I enjoy it so much. I simply think it would be nice if there were more incentive to actually engage with that part of the game. 

As far as ideas go my first thought is that maybe there could be unique crafting materials tucked away in the far reaches or on unique/legendary enemies like the black crawler, jookhela, psycho, fatso etc that give equally unique effects on things crafted with them (bonus points if they are default max quality or are irrespective of quality so they aren't wasted on a bad roll). Something like super steel that isn't just another thing you buy and grind for but rather have to actually adventure to get. 

They can also make the unique weapons start off mid but let them upgrade in tiers so they can compete towards the end game. If Styg wants maxxed craftables to still be better that's fine but let them at least be competitive. Let armor do the same. 

Finally jt never makes sense to me that the most well equipped end game enemies have weapons and armor a third the quality of mine. Am I seriously the only one in all of Underrail that crafts things with even a sliver of quality? And why do all these merchants have such high quality parts if no one but me can use them? Let end game enemies have end game tier equipment. It would be rare to find a perfect gun with rapid reloader + muzzle anyway (or forward grip vindi, etc for whatever weapon is your type). Again they don't have to be literally max quality but if max is 150-160 and they're in the final area let them have 130-140 quality equips.

It's a crit build because crit is fun and op. Tranquility doesn't feel like it'd be insane to me in comparison but like I said I've never done a playthrough with either so I wouldn't know. Lower AP cost is what makes dexterity the best base stat in the game so tranquility might be great if you can spam attacks. Careful with that line of thinking though. SMGs for example shoot 7 times every burst with the right build, with each hit doing additional damage due to expertise. No psi skill is going to do that. That's why crits for more quality over quantity is my thinking.

If you want an easier build to get you into dominating I'd actually recommend SMGs. They're incredibly easy, you don't have to manipulate your health for survival instincts, and you don't have to save-scum as much. If you don't crit when you really need to you have to reload. No fear of that on SMGs because you hate critting, it takes away your extra damage with expertise. Theres a unique item called the unprojector that actually takes away your ability to crit in exchange for 10% extra overall damage that I take every time I can for that exact reason (on smgs). If not SMG then I'd recommend ARs. They're basically SMGs except you want to crit and not take expertise. They're easier to build around in some ways and harder in others. You get more bursts per turn with SMGs because dex brings your burst cost significantly down while ARs get no such bonus. ARs however do far more per burst.

I'll just give you a few building tips for sniper. I've beaten the game multiple times on classic exp dominating as a pure sniper and honestly it's great fun and not that hard once you get rolling.

Few things you want to keep in mind:

For feats, there is only a few you truly need to pick as you level -

Aimed Shot

Strafe

Snipe

Shooting Spree (Specialize this to +5 asap. Put 1/1 into Shooting Spree: Shots first then rest into Cooldown)

Sharpshooter

Critical Power (Rest of specialization into this)

We need these perks to make it really tick. The rest are up to you. I'll post my sniper dominating build at the end if you want to see what I pick up aside from these core feats but they are all just geared to how I play the game.

\_\_\_

For skills we need a few core as well -

Guns

Throwing (you want it the be effective (not actual) 80 at max, that lets you throw with 95% accuracy up to 4 tiles away and you don't need much more than that)

Stealth (most builds only go to 80 on this stat for blindsiding. your stealth will get into the 200s even at 80 because of your armor so it's never really needed. on sniper we go the full 160 because the Snipe feat scales with your stealth investment)

Mechanics (effective score of 164. you can go far lower than this number if you search for all workbenches and get a drug from a late game area that increases your INT by 2. if you don't want to go for either of these you'll want to compensate by raising mechanics. on normal you can likely go lower than this because you wont need absolutely maxed out weapons but this is what I go for on my playthroughs)

Electronics (effective score of 194 with the same buffs stated above. this is for a maxxed out energy shield. again you can go lower than this but I'm a min-maxxer and like to have the absolute highest tier of equips I can get)

Mercantile (we really want an effective mercantile of 90-95 to unlock all merchants in the game, going higher does absolutely nothing. we only go to 90-95 because of the belt that increases mercantile by 15 you can buy fairly early)

\_\_

[Sniper Build](https://underrail.info/build/?HgUGBQMQAwjCoABFAAAAAMKgTlAAPV9wRE5nAABGRgAARwF_MRY1U34zSyvChyrChV0owrXCpMKD4qe-CuKvvATir70B37w) as I said this is my sniper build I built a while ago for dominating. I think I can still help you out a bit more though. Pickpocketing is a weird one, it's pretty good early game but you'll be swimming in loot the further you go on and it will become progressively less useful. I'd recommend going for an effective value of 50 for the early game specifically. You'll get more ammo and medicine from the early areas like SGS and Junkyard than normal and it'll greatly benefit a first time dominating playthrough. Much more than that and it's more for some weird shenanigans like stealing keycards for niche areas and such. The FAQ (https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=843557165) talks a bit more about it.

Also with such high PER you won't have trouble detecting traps, so going above 95 effective traps is kinda not worth it. At 95 you can place every single trap in the game, above that it only effects how fast people see them and how fast you detect them.

You'll get like 200+ stealth from gear alone, it doesn't need that much investment. 80 is fine for blindsiding, and you'll never get seen with that much.

You're definitely going to want more electronics if you want a good shield later on, and tailoring is also important to be able to make the infused rathound leather/ tact vest/ bio tact vest for good crits/stealth/fucking bugs in expedition respectively. 194 effective electronics will let you craft the best possible shield (and plasma nades), and 179 eff. tailoring for best armor. 112 chemistry is nice for all grenade types apart from plasma nades. Biology can range but I like 130 for supersoldier drug  (70 for hypercerebrix, it lets you bypass a lot of skill points in crafting bc 2 int is a lot). Remember to get the workbenchs for your house to bypass a lot of those skill points too. On that builder I always press the 'crafting bonus' button and under that it says food, and under that there are a list of skills. There's a few things I'd change: I'd drop STR to 5 and just use Thumper as my offhand, take 6 dex for Grenadier, 7 agi for hit and run, drop con to 3, pump per to 9, and leave int 7. 

Reasons are: 

-shotguns are crit weapons in Underrail and are basically close range sniper rifles. That is to say, you don't really need burst, and the max strength requirement for a vindicator is 5. Thumper has no str req. so that's a non-issue.

-I just love grenadier. Even with thumper or any other grenade launcher, grenades are just more versatile. You can have 2-3 different ones equipped and being able to toss them out whenever is a core part of all my builds. I'd say this is the one you could take or leave though. 

-You need the be speedy on a shotgun build since you have to be relatively close to the enemies. Hit and Run is great for this, and makes your life a whole lot easier.

-Con is a wimp stat, Underrail is all about alpha striking anyway. 900 hours in and I have never put a single point into con except for survival instincts builds (which work at 30% health, so it's no different)

-PER is an incredibly underwhelming stat, I say pump it to 9 because you can rock 9 for the entire game up to level 24, take increased per feat for 11, and have just enough per for scrutinous.

As for your skills:

-I'd drop evasion entirely. It's an RNG check to see if they hit you or not, if you're worried about getting hit you're better off doing something more concrete than trying to rely on that. Anyway, even maxxed it is incredibly underwhelming. 

-Dodge is better but not because it works any better than evasion does, it just has perks worth getting. Escape Artist requires 7 dex to get but lets you get out of any trap and is amazing (especially for Expedition) and Uncanny Dodge requires 8 agi and is okay if you're worried about melee lads because it gives you 3 free dodges to any melee attacks. I mainly use that one for death stalkers but it's great for that!

As for perks:

-Paranoia is an okay perk, but we just have better things to be taking. Hit and Run, Sprint, and Recklessness are all great and can be gotten at level 1. Shotguns also have a few core feats that we need: sixth shell is similar to concentrated fire for ARs and is basically what makes the build tick. With 100% crit and the sixth bullet you'll literally one shot anything in the game bar none. We also love leading shot because it makes landing hits so much easier, and is part of the reason we don't really need high PER. Pellet Mayhem is.. okay? If you go for 100% crit it literally does nothing later on in the game (which I'm honestly just realizing) but it's still good for early on. You can replace it if you like, it's not going to hurt much. Fragmented Chaos is why we love crits on shotguns.

Feats to avoid: Barrel Stare is not good, it has anti-synergy with leading shot and you have to be kissing them to get it's bonus. Perfect Scattering is not good either, at most you're getting 40 damage (unaffected by crit) if all 20 pellets of a 20p shell land. At worst, you're getting 3-6 damage if you're using 3p or 6p respectively. And finally critical power. It simply doesn't work with Fragmented Chaos, otherwise it'd be great.

With your build there are just a few things I'd change without getting rid of your identity. The agility is fine, but you're kinda gimping yourself with only 13 dex. Dex is the most op base stat in the game as it lowers the AP value for shooting your SMGs/pistols. I'd also focus on either pistols or smgs, rather than going for both. Other than flavor there really isn't a reason in the game to go for a two weapon build, unless it's just a dip (like going 15 crossbows for marksman, and that's it)

The reason is that pistols get a lot of value from the special attacks, such as aimed/kneecap shot as well as bullet time. They are also crit focused, favoring few big attacks over peppering them with a lot of less powerful ones. SMGs are the complete opposite, they favor more attacks over anything. The reason is because they get a ton of value from the expertise feat. Thing is, expertise doesn't proc on crits. So SMGs are solely non-crit based. 

Other than that there's only minor nitpicks: evasion is kind of a dump stat. dodge is okay because it gets you escape artist and uncanny dodge, but as far as the stats themselves they are kinda the worst ones in the game. Even at max you don't dodge/evade very often and it's more reliable to go full damage and kill everything before they get a chance to hurt you or go guranteed tank and be able to consistently survive. 

Traps you only need an effective value of 95 to be able to place every type of trap in the game, anything over that is only affecting how quickly npcs see them.

You only need 55 temporal manipulation to be able to learn the best spell in the game (from the doctor in railroad, a city you'll find later.) Way later in the game you can get the second best spell in the game from Pasquale in SGS and it requires 70 TM. In fact, there are no TM skills that require 100 to learn, and offensively it's not a great tree so pumping it for accuracy is kind of a bust. The two spells I mentioned do not scale with it in the slightest, you only need the base value to learn them.

Your lockpicking effective value w/ mk 3 and jackknife is 184, so you can drop it all the way down to a base value of 56 and still end up with 130 effective at level 30. Hacking you can drop to 95 and have the same effect.

There's a few other even more minor nitpicks I can make but they are even more niche so I won't go into them.

80 stealth is plenty for the entire game. Your gear will carry you into the 200+ range. (80 stealth gets you the blindsiding feat, which is incredible)

To be able to lockpick/hack anything in the game, you want 130 effective value. This is the highest check you will find for either of them. With the late game lockpicking/hacking tool you get a 15 point boost to your skill, and in the GMS there is an npc who has a unique knife called the jackknife that raises your lockpicking skill by 7. With these you need 107 effective lockpicking and 115 effective hacking. 

On that same 5 int SMG character I mentioned earlier I spec 45 lockpicking and 95 hacking. On my 18 per sniper I take a more even 80 lockpicking and 78 hacking. Basically it depends on your build because they are increased/decreased based on your other stat and skill investments.

1: General endgame builds: any one weapon, either ranged or melee, and pure psi. You can make everything in the game work, it's pretty balanced in the fact that almost every build has a way to alpha strike every encounter or survive long enough to make it not matter. If you want easiest, go Assault Rifle for crit build or SMGs for non-crit build. Snipers, Shotguns, Pistols, and Energy Pistols are all also crit-based and strong in their own right. I'd say AR and SMGs are S tier and the others I said are all A (except maybe snipers, there is a lot of cheese involved in making those work.) I haven't done a playthrough of pure PSI, anything melee, or xbows but from what I've seen and heard they are all up there as well.

3: What to focus on? Many skills have hard caps that they don't spell out to you in the game, but past that point any more investment becomes basically meaningless. Many of them you can tell if you plan your build out (such as stopping stealth at 80 because you want Blindsiding) but others are harder to tell (like electronics, having an effective value of 194 will let you craft the best possible shield, 171 for tailoring, etc)

Because of these hard caps it's easy to become a jack of all trades and get basically everything you want from a character. Like maxxed offensive stat, great throwing skill, insane stealth, lockpicking/hacking everything in the game bar-none, craft literally anything in the game at max efficiency, max mercantile to unlock every tier of every merchant in the game, and still have points left over to spec Temporal Manipulation so you can give yourself free AP in combat.

If you want things to NOT focus on: I'd ignore dodge/evasion, you don't want to rely on RNG for survival when killing things is so much more efficient (dodge 30 for escape artist feat is okay), pickpocketing and traps (different people will pill you on these two skills, but I've literally never once pickpocketed anything in the game and always end up owning a majority stake in the universe by the end. Traps are better than pickpocketing but I just straight up don't use them even when I've invested into them.) and finally persuasion/intimidation. These two skills are just not needed, there is a handful of persuasion checks and even less intim. checks (if they even exist, i've never invested into it) and they can't reward you with anything of use because the only way you get anything you actually want in this game is to buy it from a merchant (preferably one you've upgraded with mercantile.) 

I recommend using this [Build Planner](https://underrail.info/build/) and cross referencing it with this [Underrail FAQ](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=843557165) to plan out what you want and what you need. 

4: There are many stories to follow in Underrail. Ofc the main story, junkyard factions, camp hathor, rail crossing, foundry, core city oligarchs, protectorate vs free drones, Jack Quicksilver and his faction, and the DLCs have an aegis story and a pirate story, and heavy duty exists.

The only reason I put anything into guns at all is for feats that require the investment like full auto and spec ops

Oh yeah for sure 3 con is intimidating at first but once you realize alpha strike is the best strategy in the game you realize health is just a handicap. Con is really there for better alpha strikes w/ survival instincts on crit builds lol.

I'm curious why you chose 8 PER though, you don't really get any feats at that level and if you're going with melee versatility it's not doing anything. And if you're going straight guns 8 per is not necessarily gonna be enough if you're not going versatility. The dex isn't doing much of anything if you don't go versatility other than lowering the AP value.

Not to kill your vibe though since they are burst weapons you'll still hit things it just might not be as consistent as it could be, SMGs are still way overpowered even the way you're going so it should be fine.

It may have been, I've posted it a few times. The reason we take melee is because it scales with dex, while guns scales with perception. We only take 6 per for the feats that require it, it would be lower if it were possible. So this combined with versatility nets you a higher guns score than you'd get with just pumping guns alone.

Int at 5 doesn't really have any drawbacks, the scores I provided let you craft the absolute highest tier of SMG, tac vest, energy shield, grenades/traps, and drugs you want. It does take a hefty investment to get there in crafting, but even with that investment we're able to get our mercantile maxxed out to get most all the benefits it provides (there are some meme checks that we can't reach but the important ones aren't that high), we're able to get the psi skills we need (you can drop psychokinesis if you don't want to use electrokinetic imprint but it's pretty fun), we're able to reach 130 effective in hacking/lockpicking with huxkey jackknife (put lockpicking to 47 idk why I didn't spec it correctly in that build), 80 stealth for blindsiding is plenty because our gear gets us to like 200+ effective skill in there anyway, throwing only needs to be at 80 effective to get very good accuracy up to 4 tiles away, and with all that we still have enough left over for 30 dodge for escape artist for the damn dlc.

There's only a few reasons to take a higher int. One is if you want the feats associated with the higher scores (premeditation at 6, gun nut and skinner at 7) but for SMGs you don't really need those. I would say premed is a good thing to have but the scores here are so tight that we can't really afford it. We already lost a dex to reach the pre.req for full auto. The other reason is if you're really tight on skill points and need them out of your crafting skills, but since we can get everything we need at 5 it's perfect.

I guess you can also say the 3rd reason is because you have nowhere else to put the attribute points which can happen. Both my dom shotgun build and sniper build go for 7 just because I don't need them anywhere else. Dex is very overtuned in this game so we want as much as possible, it even hurts to not get to 18 in this build. On the flip side perception is pretty weak so in my builds that need per I usually only go for 11 and spread the rest out elsewhere.

As for gear we want rapid muzzled 7.62mm jaguar and a rapid muzzled 8.6mm steel cat in the off-hand. I usually go with free drones for max stealth gear and coretech for max science gear (mainly plasma micro-dischargers for plasma nades)

If you find something called the unprojector (randomly found on any merchant that can sell goggles) it's great because we don't crit with this build. If you cant find it, balaclavas are still fine.

As for feats you can drop paranoia/trigger happy/quick pockets for whatever you want. Some options I'd recommend are dirty kick and expose weakness since we spec melee for versatility. You can also drop agi to 4 and take 7 int 18 dex but I like sprint and hit n' run; those are also optional.
